evidence:
The frozen workbook Quality Checks row 21/check 20 and its Internal Quality Checks annotation require a committed static reference without variability on pinned values; the frozen skill quality-checks.md:87-88 specifically requires deterministic seeds and fixed-clock graded rules. Independently executed git show for every task file at commit 4ec94aecf74dbbc8a6328ebab44ced846b5f8b96: all 37 Git blobs match the frozen bytes, manifest and committed-reference.json. The cited raw-index artifact committed-reference.json hashes to 2802edeafe7945c1ba06baf899f0e2fa54db60f7a9772cff9b5a1fb78778ddb5, matching its current index entry. All 34 frozen rule/template hashes and current QC policy/README hashes also match their manifest entries.

In frozen task/solution/solve.sh:35-36 the installer copies its co-located app and resets only the disposable database; it does not generate or fetch the reference. src/db.js:14-19 reads the shipped co-located seed/constants; :122-179 seeds within a transaction using supplied IDs and reference_moment, with the nonempty-users guard at :123-124. Shipped and solution seed hashes both equal 1b39015461a7a4f23b835aeea9584caffd0266c64d394778376cbd6c8a18bcf7. src/index.js:49,180-185 uses the stored clock for referral calculations; rescission uses its supplied stored effective date at :384-401. src/rules.js:17-46,105-149 uses explicit UTC date inputs and deterministic integer formulas. bootstrap.js:28-30 only proxies loopback HTTP; no boot-time external data fetch changes a pinned figure. The template deployer likewise copies committed local files.

Actual isolated Docker probe: python -B qc/runs/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r3/per-row-review/evidence/20/run-probe.py exited 0 against image sha256:958902dedd30475f2f1e94c046b1b718b0c76d18cc733486bb81dfdbf61f3bc6, network none, frozen app read-only, private tmpfs databases. Two fresh real SQLite databases under mocked clocks 1999-01-01 and 2041-12-31 and time zones Pacific/Kiritimati/America/Adak produced identical rows across 15 tables (row digest 1d575f2426f00861bbecc3c9eb6b9dc538454234448872f1deee7a847babb94c) and identical derived composition/headroom/referral/signing/equity figures (digest bfe96425c4aabbe6bce16c6b6ed9f0dd1ed88f853499e46bd46e20cc72e9cb65). Re-seeding and reopening each database left rows unchanged; seed-time Math.random/crypto.randomBytes were configured to throw and were not needed. Exact command, input hashes, image, row counts and observations are in evidence/20/observations.json (SHA256 53670c4c0f1661b3a1c24d361e28a7b02b3193f3d7fdf3f0b6f5e76c818fb4f3) and stdout.json (SHA256 8e7c7f4a54acdb430bd6cc207c648144af7b1677482aa93855eeb68745388944).

Broken alternative tested: supplying wall-clock time to referralVested makes both seeded referrals change from 500000 to 1000000 vested cents across these clocks, whereas the actual fixed-clock path remains 500000/1000000. Such a reference could pass a single-date smoke check but is detected here. Conforming alternative considered: random session tokens and newly allocated record IDs must not be treated as unstable pinned seed values. The current random calls (index.js:50,99; change-sets.js:87) serve those unpinned values; public rules:238 permit chosen revision IDs and :436 prescribe no generated record format. This is row-specific source and finite SQLite/rule evidence, not a full app judge run, Oracle score, model grade or portal result. No unresolved row-20 defect or required row-20 measurement gap remains.
